🌎 BEYOND THE 956

British actor and comedian Russell Brand was convicted Thursday of rape and sexual assault in a London court, and was taken into custody ahead of his sentencing.

A jury at Southwark Crown Court found Brand, 51, guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The jury cleared him of two other rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault.

The charges involved six women and dated back to incidents between 1999 and 2009. Brand had denied all of the charges and pleaded not guilty.

Judge Joel Bennathan denied Brand's request for bail and remanded him into custody, warning that he faces a significant prison sentence when he returns to court for sentencing on Monday, November 9.

London Metropolitan Police Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy praised the women who came forward, calling the conviction a testament to their extraordinary courage, resilience, and determination.

The women in the case are entitled to lifelong anonymity under UK law, and their names have not been published.

Update — November 9, 2026

On Monday, November 9, Judge Joel Bennathan sentenced Brand, 51, to 10 years and six months in prison at Southwark Crown Court in London, following his November 5 conviction on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Brand will serve two-thirds of the sentence in custody before being released on licence, the court said.

Before sentencing, four of the women in the case gave victim impact statements to the court. The judge praised the determination and bravery of the women who came forward, and said Brand had acted as though fame put him above the rules ordinary people live by.

Metropolitan Police Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy said Brand "has been held accountable for his crimes" and that he hoped the outcome provides the victims some measure of closure. The Metropolitan Police said it is still investigating two further rape allegations against Brand. Brand has denied all charges and pleaded not guilty; no appeal had been reported as of publication.

Update — November 12, 2026

On Tuesday, November 10, London’s Metropolitan Police confirmed that several people contacted its investigation team during and since Brand’s trial to provide information or report potential criminal allegations, and that detectives are assessing the information as part of their ongoing enquiries, according to PEOPLE and other outlets. No new charges have been announced in connection with the latest reports, which are allegations being assessed, not proven offences. The force’s investigation into two further rape allegations against Brand remains ongoing, with files submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service. Brand’s former partner Jemima Goldsmith also publicly accused him of “violence, coercive control and abuse” during their relationship; that is a public claim, not a charge. No appeal had been reported as formally filed as of publication.

Sources: WorldStar (@worldstar) on Instagram; Metropolitan Police; Reuters; USA Today. Update sources: USA Today, Nov. 9, 2026; Associated Press via WHRO, Nov. 9, 2026; Metropolitan Police statement, Nov. 9, 2026; PEOPLE, Nov. 10, 2026; Metropolitan Police statement, Nov. 10, 2026.

Update — November 13, 2026

Six more women have accused Brand of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour, in an investigation by The Times and The Sunday Times published Thursday, November 12. The claims, which the outlets said span a decade, include an allegation that Brand continued having sex with a 19-year-old woman after she asked him to stop because she was in pain, and an allegation from a woman who said he penetrated her with his finger after inviting her to his hotel following a show in San Francisco in 2013. The outlets said the claims could not be published until Brand's trial ended, to avoid prejudicing the proceedings, and that most of the six women first approached journalists after the September 2023 investigation by The Times, The Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches. Separately, Page Six reported November 10 that a woman in the United States has come forward with a new allegation against Brand and is in communication with attorney Gloria Allred about her options; her identity and the details of her allegation have not been publicly disclosed. No new criminal charges or civil proceedings have been announced in connection with either report, and the claims are allegations, not findings. Brand has denied wrongdoing.

Update sources: Page Six, Nov. 10, 2026; Page Six, Nov. 12, 2026; Internewscast, Nov. 12, 2026.

title: Beyond the 956: Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault, taken into custody
